title-group.article-title: Single-cell multi-omics of the aging brain

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Aging reshapes the cellular composition of the mammalian brain, but the molecular programs that drive this process remain incompletely mapped.

sec.title: Materials and methods
sec.p: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on 12,000 cells from aged and young mouse brains and applied a multi-omics integration pipeline.
Libraries were prepared with the 10x Genomics platform and sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 instrument.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Aged brains showed a 2.4-fold increase in senescent microglia and reduced oligodendrocyte progenitor numbers.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: These results suggest that senescence programs shape the aging brain microenvironment and may be reversible.

sec.title: Limitations
sec.p: Our study has limitations: only two age groups were profiled, and the findings may not generalize to human tissue.
